title: Pre-Hartal Rush: The Day Before
content: The day before a hartal (bandh) is the single most profitable day for a Kerala kirana store, if stocked correctly. Dairy demand rises 80% — customers buy 2-3 days of milk and eggs in advance because dairy suppliers do not deliver on hartal day. Staples (rice, coconut oil, flour) rise 60% as families stock up for a day at home. Snacks and chips rise 65% because people snack heavily on hartal days. Beverages (tea, coffee) rise 45%. Spices rise 30% for home cooking. Strategy: identify hartal news by 8 PM the evening before. If confirmed, place emergency orders with all daily-cycle suppliers immediately. Do not wait for the normal morning order window. If Amul Distributor cannot deliver on hartal day, request pre-hartal delivery.

title: Hartal Day: Near-Zero Demand and Security
content: On hartal day itself, store sales drop to approximately 8% of normal levels. Most Kerala kirana stores open only briefly (7-9 AM) during hartals, if at all. Do not place any supplier orders on hartal day — no deliveries will happen. The key action on hartal day is stock-taking and preparation for the post-hartal rush. Hartals organised by major political parties (CPM, Congress, BJP) in Kerala have close to 100% compliance in urban areas like Thrissur and Ernakulam. District-specific hartals may have lower compliance. Hartals called in the evening for the next day typically give 12-14 hours of warning — use this window to stock up.

title: Post-Hartal: Recovery Demand
content: The day after a hartal sees demand approximately 15% above normal across all categories. Customers who avoided shopping during the hartal return. Dairy demand recovers fastest — milk and eggs see 20-25% above-normal sales. Replenish shelves first thing in the morning. Contact your daily suppliers by 6 AM post-hartal to confirm delivery schedules. Some suppliers may be running behind due to hartal backlog. Palakkad suppliers are particularly slow to recover post-hartal due to road conditions. Prioritise Amul (Thrissur) for dairy recovery orders.

title: Transport Strikes: Supplier Risk Assessment
content: Transport strikes (lorry bandh, autorickshaw strike) in Kerala affect supplier delivery reliability differently from general hartals. Lorry strikes impact Palakkad Agro Traders severely — 90% of their deliveries use lorry transport from Palakkad and Coimbatore. During lorry strikes, switch all staples and spices orders to Metro Cash & Carry Kochi (uses own vans) or Sri Krishna Wholesale (local Thrissur delivery). Amul Distributor uses dedicated Amul refrigerated vehicles — minimal impact from general transport strikes. Metro Cash & Carry is the most resilient to transport disruption. Never rely on Palakkad Agro Traders during a transport strike, even if they are the cheapest option.

title: How to Monitor Hartal Risk in Kerala
content: Kerala hartal announcements typically come through these channels: (1) Local WhatsApp groups of shop owners associations; (2) Kerala news websites: Mathrubhumi, Manorama Online, Kerala Kaumudi; (3) Twitter/X handles of major political parties CPM and Congress Kerala; (4) Radio — AIR Thiruvananthapuram and Mathrubhumi Radio. Announcement to implementation is usually 12-24 hours. Flash hartals (called on same day) happen but are rare — usually in response to political events. Set up Google Alerts for 'hartal Kerala' and 'bandh Kerala'. Shopkeepers in Thrissur district also share alerts via the Thrissur District Vyapari Vyavasayi Ekopana Samithi WhatsApp group.

title: Seasonal Rain and Supply Chain Disruption
content: Kerala's monsoon season (June-August) causes predictable supply disruptions. Heavy rain days reduce supplier on-time rates: Palakkad Agro Traders drops from 71% to below 50% on-time delivery during heavy monsoon. Roads between Palakkad and Thrissur (NH 544) frequently flood during heavy rain. Metro Cash & Carry (Kochi) is more reliable in rain as Kochi roads are better maintained. Rainy days also shift consumer behaviour: Tea demand rises 30%, snacks rise 25%, but overall footfall drops 10%. Reduce perishable orders by 15% before a heavy rain day. Stock up on long-shelf-life beverages and snacks instead.

title: Emergency Order Thresholds: When to Act Immediately
content: Emergency orders in a Kerala kirana store should be placed immediately (same day, regardless of order cycle) when: (1) Any perishable item (milk, eggs) falls below 2 days remaining stock; (2) Any item with high hartal demand (milk, rice, snacks) falls below 3 days when a hartal is confirmed within 24 hours; (3) Any item drops to zero stock (out-of-stock costs both revenue and customer loyalty); (4) A festival is 3 days away and festival-critical items are below the 7-day threshold. Emergency orders always justify the 15% premium cost from non-cycle orders. The revenue loss from a stockout far exceeds the cost premium.
